public_rationale: The records establish both customer purchases and investment by a cloud supplier in an AI lab. Neither establishes the claimed dependence of substantial AI demand on that funding. Real payments alone cannot settle the financing question, and an investment relationship alone cannot prove that independent demand is absent.
limitations: Ramp observes its own customer base, not the entire market.
No causal estimate of demand without hyperscaler funding was found.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: AI demand doesn't really exist without hyperscalers effectively paying themselves through investments in AI labs.

statement.excerpt: Okay, all jokes aside, there’s very clearly a problem here with AI demand, in the sense that it doesn’t really exist without hyperscalers paying themselves to do so.

our_interpretation: The plain reading is that substantial commercial AI demand depends on hyperscaler investments funding purchases from those same hyperscalers.
This is stronger than saying that circular financing exists or that investment exceeds customer spending.
For this ongoing observation, use April–June 2026, the latest completed calendar quarter that could be publicly reported before the post.
Customer payments establish demand, but do not by themselves establish whether that demand would survive withdrawal of hyperscaler funding.
criteria.support_condition: Evidence tracing customer spending and financing shows that commercially substantial AI demand depends on hyperscalers funding their own customers.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Evidence establishes substantial commercial AI purchases financed independently of hyperscaler investments, with enough information to distinguish independent demand from investment-funded purchases.
